notes.summary: Primary-source audit of permitted bounded Hermitian comparison/existence and canonical local calculus; no singular comparison or positive v_- assumption.
notes.detailedSummary: Checks the bounded contact inequality and strict exponential comparison in nonclosed backgrounds, continuous scalar existence with density vanishing at one point, removable psh extension, and operator scaling. These are explicitly permitted analytic dependencies; their arbitrary-singular applications are reconstructed in subsequent notes.
notes.text:
Analytic dependencies and primary-source audit.

Throughout, D=dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial, every potential is its genuine canonical upper representative, and MA denotes the stipulated corrected non-pluripolar product.

The indispensable global statements were checked in primary papers. Guedj–Lu, Quasi-plurisubharmonic envelopes 3, arXiv:2107.01938v1, Lemma 1.2 (p.5), gives the bounded contact inequality in a smooth semipositive background. Proposition 1.12 and Corollary 1.14 (pp.8–9) give strict comparison with a strict analytic barrier. Only the bounded specialization with barrier rho=0 is used: for a smooth Hermitian background h and bounded genuine h-psh u,v,
  exp(-lambda v) MA_h(v) >= exp(-lambda u) MA_h(u), lambda>0,
implies v<=u. On {u<v-epsilon}, the inequality implies MA_h(u)<=exp(-lambda epsilon)MA_h(v-epsilon); bounded strict comparison applies, and epsilon decreases to zero. The background is strictly positive, rho=0 is a smooth strict barrier, and the lower-bound hypotheses are automatic. No uniform lower mass hypothesis is used.

The contact inequality with lower potential A constant and upper potential U>=A gives
  1_{U=A} h^N <= 1_{U=A} MA_h(U).
This includes the whole level set, not merely its interior, and allows nonclosed h.

Nguyen, The complex Monge–Ampere type equation on compact Hermitian manifolds and applications, arXiv:1501.00891v1, Theorem 2.1 and Lemma 2.3 (p.13), were checked for nonnegative L^p densities, p>1, of positive integral. No positive lower bound is required. They provide a continuous bounded solution and bounded uniqueness for a positive exponent. Existence below is used only on P1 with density H ell^(sigma d), continuous, nonzero, and vanishing at one point.

The normalization conversion is explicit. Nguyen’s operator is twice ours. Apply its exponent-one theorem with background 2 sigma a omega_1 and unknown U=sigma q. The resulting equation is precisely a omega_1+Dq=H ell^(sigma d)exp(sigma q)omega_1; the relative density is H ell^(sigma d)/a. Guedj–Lu’s operator is 4 pi times ours. Replace each source potential by our potential/(4 pi), and its exponent by 4 pi times our exponent. This transports contact and strict comparison without changing the background forms.

Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012 version, Chapter I, Theorems 5.7, 5.8 and 5.24 (pp.39–45), were checked: locally uniformly upper bounded psh families have psh usc supremums; a positive distributional complex Hessian determines a unique canonical psh representative; and a psh function on the complement of a closed pluripolar set, locally bounded above near it, extends uniquely. The removal argument uses a smooth analytic divisor and verifies the necessary residual upper bound. Adding a local potential of a constant closed form dominating a smooth background reduces the local extension to this statement; positivity in the original nonclosed background is checked separately.

Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Acta Math.149 (1982), Theorem 4.1 (pp.14–16) and bounded monotone calculus were inspected. Their comparison is local for bounded psh functions with the required boundary inequality. No global closed-background comparison is inferred for a nonclosed form. Local corrected products are expanded around a closed dominating form. Their bounded identities hold term by term. Locality on truncation superlevels and omission of pluripolar mass are properties of the stipulated genuine non-pluripolar construction. In particular, on {r>A}, MA_h(max(r,A))=MA_h(r), including when r has further poles.

These are permitted, source-checked analytic dependencies, not newly proved global theorems. Subsequent notes reconstruct the new singular and product arguments. No arbitrary-singular strict domination theorem, bounded mass property on Y, equality of nonclosed total masses, or assumption v_-(h)>0 is used.

Primary URLs: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.01938 ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.00891 ; https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf ; https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf . Retrieved passages and failed initial access attempts are retained in source_receipts.json. No private proposed proof, previous report, candidate article, or credential file was read. notes.summary: Divisorial removal with arbitrary additional poles; theta and eta are strictly positive and nonclosed whenever b is nonconstant, for every specified Y.
notes.detailedSummary: Constructs the unique canonical eta-psh residual, separately proves positivity across D, establishes equality of actual non-pluripolar measures, and proves the bounded-residual/ordinary-type equivalence. Arbitrary residuals need not have finite mass.
notes.text:
Divisorial removal and background assertions: target B.

Let Y be any connected compact Hermitian k-fold with integral kappa^k=1, k>=1. The product X=P1 x Y is connected, compact, and of dimension N=k+1. The form dW=omega_1 wedge kappa^k is a smooth strictly positive probability volume. Set K=a+d, theta=K omega_1+b kappa and eta=a omega_1+b kappa.

Both backgrounds are smooth and strictly positive: their horizontal blocks are respectively K omega_1 and a omega_1, and their vertical blocks are b kappa. Compactness gives domination of a positive multiple of any fixed Hermitian metric. They are big using the genuine potential 0 and nef using the positive representative theta+epsilon h or eta+epsilon h itself.

For nonconstant b,
  d theta=d eta=db wedge kappa+b d_Y kappa.
The two terms have different horizontal real degrees, respectively one and zero, and cannot cancel. Since db is nonzero somewhere and kappa is positive and nonzero for k>=1, db wedge kappa is nonzero. Thus both backgrounds are genuinely nonclosed, irrespective of closedness of kappa.

In z=Z1/Z0, omega_1=D log(1+|z|^2) has mass one and psi=-d log(1+|z|^2). Near p={Z0=0}, with t=Z0/Z1,
  psi=d log|t|^2-d log(1+|t|^2).
For our operator, D log|t|^2=delta_0: D=(Delta/(4 pi))dx dy and Delta log|t|^2=4 pi delta_0, as follows by integration on a small circle. Consequently
  D psi=d[D]-d omega_1,
  theta+D psi=eta+d[D].
Its canonical value on D is -infinity.

Suppose v is genuine theta-psh and v<=psi+C. Off D put r=v-psi. There r is quasi-psh, r<=C, and eta+Dr=theta+Dv>=0. On a coordinate ball choose a constant closed positive form beta>=eta and a smooth Q with DQ=beta. Then r+Q is psh off D and locally bounded above near D. By n1 it has a unique canonical psh extension R. Define r=R-Q. These local definitions glue because they agree off D and canonical representatives with the same distribution agree everywhere.

Positivity across D must be checked. Write P=DR>=0. Then eta+Dr=P-(beta-eta) has measure coefficients and is positive off D. Its coefficient-measure restriction to D is 1_D P, since the smooth form beta-eta gives D zero mass. Therefore both its restrictions to D and its complement are positive, proving eta+Dr>=0 globally. The upper bound r<=C also extends. No lower bound is required, so arbitrary additional poles are permitted.

Off D the identity v=psi+r holds. On D both sides canonically equal -infinity. Conversely, every genuine eta-psh r gives the genuine theta-psh potential psi+r, since
  theta+D(psi+r)=eta+Dr+d[D]>=0.
The sum is not identically -infinity because the polar sets of nontrivial quasi-psh functions have zero volume. Its residual is unique: agreement off D fixes its distribution and hence its canonical representative on D.

On X minus D, psi is smooth and the two total local backgrounds agree. Corrected local product identities and non-pluripolar truncation therefore give
  MA_theta(psi+r)=MA_eta(r)
there. Neither actual non-pluripolar measure charges D, so equality holds globally, as possibly infinite measures. Further poles are handled by the same non-pluripolar convention. No wedge with the divisor current is taken.

Finally psi+r has ordinary bounded type relative to psi exactly when r is bounded. Mutual comparisons give finite upper and lower bounds for r off D, and canonical extension preserves them on D. Conversely a bounded residual supplies the mutual comparisons globally, interpreted at common canonical poles.

notes.summary: Exact full-product model, comparisons, smaller-background envelope, and finite positive product for any compact Hermitian factor.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves the prescribed piecewise formula, psi<=phi<=psi+C_*, stabilized model envelopes, and P_eta(-psi)=phi-psi with its bounded extension. Computes MA_theta(phi)=N K 1_{|z|^2<R}b^k dW without factor symmetry, closedness, or a bounded mass property.
notes.text:
Exact ordinary model: target A.

Keep every Y allowed in n2. Set R=a/d and C_*=K log(K/d)-a log(a/d). Define phi=0 for s=|z|^2<=R and phi=a log s+C_*-K log(1+s) for s>R, with canonical value -infinity on D.

The exterior value is zero at R and its derivative a/s-K/(1+s) vanishes there. That derivative is negative for s>R. Hence phi<=0, sup phi=0, and the matching is C^1 away from D, with no boundary-circle atom.

The bounded residual F is defined explicitly, rather than by subtracting infinities:
  F(s)=d log(1+s), s<=R;
  F(s)=a log(s/(1+s))+C_*, s>R;
  F|_D=C_*.
The values and derivatives match. Both branches increase from 0 to C_*. Positivity of C_* follows from C_*/d=(R+1)log(R+1)-R log R, which increases from zero for R>0. Thus, including common poles,
  psi<=phi<=psi+C_*.
Near D, F=C_*-a log(1+|t|^2), so its extension is smooth there.

Distributional differentiation gives
  K omega_1+D phi=K 1_{s<R}omega_1+d[p].
Inside the circle D phi=0; outside, the total horizontal current is D(a log s)=0 away from the excluded point 0 and p. Matching derivatives exclude circle mass, and the local expression at p has logarithmic coefficient d. Therefore
  theta+D phi=K 1_{s<R}omega_1+b kappa+d[D]>=0.
This proves genuine theta-psh positivity and eta-psh positivity of F. Removing D and expanding the bounded product leaves precisely one horizontal factor and k vertical factors:
  MA_theta(phi)=MA_eta(F)=N K 1_{s<R}b^k dW.
There is neither circle nor divisor mass. Its exact mass is N K integral_{s<R}b^k omega_1, finite and strictly positive. No derivative of kappa, closedness, or mass property on Y enters.

To prove the full-product envelope bound, let v be any genuine theta-psh potential with v<=0 and v<=psi+C. For each fixed y its restriction v_y is K omega_1-psh on P1 or identically -infinity. This restriction follows by locally adding a closed dominating potential, convolving the psh function, and restricting. Smoothness of the original background makes the convolution error uniformly o(1); passing to the canonical restriction proves horizontal positivity for every nontrivial slice. Identically polar slices satisfy the desired bound automatically.

On the exterior disk {s>R} together with p, the difference
  v_y-[a log s+C_*-K log(1+s)]
is subharmonic away from p. By n2 it equals r_y-a log(s/(1+s))-C_* and is bounded above near p. It extends subharmonically across p. On the boundary s=R its upper values are <=0, because v<=0 and phi=0. The disk maximum principle gives v_y<=phi. Inside the circle this follows directly from v<=0. Thus v<=phi on the entire product without an action on Y.

Every candidate for P_theta(min(psi+C,0)) satisfies that bound, which persists under usc regularization. For C>=C_* the constructed phi is itself a candidate. Consequently
  P_theta(min(psi+C,0))=phi for C>=C_*,
  P_theta[psi](0)=phi.
Every candidate for P_theta(min(phi+C,0)) is also <=0 and dominated by psi plus a constant. Since phi is a candidate for C>=0, these envelopes equal phi as well. Therefore P_theta[phi](0)=phi with sup phi=0: the full-product ordinary model property.

The smaller-background envelope is
  P_eta(-psi)=F.
Here -psi is finite off D and +infinity on D. Every genuine eta-psh candidate r is globally upper bounded by compactness. Thus v=psi+r is theta-psh, <=0, and dominated by psi plus a constant. The preceding disk argument gives r<=F off D, then everywhere by canonical extension. Conversely F is eta-psh and <=-psi because phi<=0. The continuous upper bound F also controls usc regularization on D, proving the formula.

notes.summary: Explicit mean-zero Green kernel and whole-family scalar asymptotics, including the actual sigma^(-1)log(c_sigma/c0) error.
notes.detailedSummary: Derives the Green identities and L^p-to-uniform bound, establishes uniform additive bounds after scalar centering, and proves uniform residual convergence. Both prescribed normalizations and the nonzero scalar-error limit follow directly, without extracting clusters.
notes.text:
Green formula and scalar asymptotics.

Integrals here are on P1 with omega_1 unless otherwise stated. Put L=-log ell and psi=-dL. In the affine chart omega_1=(1/pi)dx dy/(1+|z|^2)^2. Its pushforward by ell=1/(1+|z|^2) is Lebesgue measure on [0,1]. Thus integral L=1, integral L^2=2, and every finite power of L is integrable.

For finite affine coordinates x,z, chordal distance squared is |x-z|^2/((1+|x|^2)(1+|z|^2)), with its usual limits at infinity. Define G(x,z)=log d_chord(x,z)^2+1, canonically -infinity on the diagonal. The normalized logarithmic identity of n2 gives
  D_xG=delta_z-omega_1.
The reciprocal coordinate checks z=infinity and excludes any extra atom. The unitary projective action on P1 preserves the chordal distance and Fubini–Study volume. Moving z to 0, the variable q=|x|^2/(1+|x|^2) is uniform on [0,1]. Therefore
  integral G(x,z)omega_1(x)=0,
  integral |G(x,z)|omega_1(x)=2/e,
  integral G(x,z)^2 omega_1(x)=1.
These also hold with x fixed and z integrated. This proves the stated constant +1 normalization; no action on Y is used.

Let Tg(x)=integral G(x,z)g(z)omega_1(z). For p>1, Holder’s inequality gives ||Tg||_infinity<=C_p||g||_p. The kernel depends continuously on x in every finite L^q norm: remove small disks about approaching poles, use uniform convergence on the complement, and estimate the omitted logarithmic tails by integral_0^epsilon |log t|^q dt. Hence Tg is continuous, and L^p convergence gives uniform convergence of Tg. For bounded g, ||Tg||_infinity<=(2/e)||g||_infinity. Fubini and the distributional Green identity give
  integral Tg omega_1=0,
  D(Tg)=(g-integral g)omega_1.
The logarithmic bounds justify these operations. A distributionally harmonic function on the compact curve is constant, by local convolution and the harmonic maximum principle. Thus T is the mean-zero inverse of D.

Set m=integral H>0, c0=a/m and g0=aH/m-a. Then w0=Tg0 is continuous, has omega_1-mean zero, and
  a omega_1+D w0=(aH/m)omega_1.
It is a genuine a omega_1-psh potential. Pull back to X and set S0=sup(psi+w0), finite and attained off D. The probability dnu0=(H/m)dW has finite M=integral_X(psi+w0)dnu0, since H is bounded and L integrable.

For each sigma>0 put W_sigma=H ell^(sigma d), with value zero at p. This continuous nonnegative density has positive integral and belongs to every L^p. The checked bounded existence theorem in n1 gives a unique continuous genuine a omega_1-psh q_sigma solving
  a omega_1+Dq_sigma=W_sigma exp(sigma q_sigma)omega_1.    (1)
Integrating this one-dimensional current gives integral W_sigma exp(sigma q_sigma)=a. This uses closedness of the base curve background only, not a nonclosed product mass identity.

Write I_sigma=integral W_sigma and Bbar_sigma=T(a W_sigma/I_sigma-a). The two bounded potentials
  q_minus=Bbar_sigma+log(a/I_sigma)/sigma-max Bbar_sigma,
  q_plus=Bbar_sigma+log(a/I_sigma)/sigma-min Bbar_sigma
have curvature (a W_sigma/I_sigma)omega_1. The first is an exponential subsolution of (1), and the second a supersolution. Bounded strict comparison gives q_minus<=q_sigma<=q_plus.

Since 0<=m-I_sigma<=sigma d||H||_infinity integral L, eventually I_sigma>=m/2 and
  0<=log(m/I_sigma)/sigma<=2d||H||_infinity/m.
The Green bound controls Bbar_sigma uniformly. Consequently Q_sigma=q_sigma-log(c0)/sigma is uniformly bounded for all sufficiently small sigma. This is an additive bound, not merely control of an exponential.

Put tau_sigma=integral Q_sigma omega_1 and w_sigma=Q_sigma-tau_sigma. Equation (1) gives
  w_sigma=Tg_sigma,
  g_sigma=c0H exp(sigma(psi+Q_sigma))-a,
  integral g_sigma=0.
The additive bound, psi<=0 and dominated convergence give g_sigma->g0 in every finite L^p. The Green estimate yields w_sigma->w0 uniformly on P1. Uniform density convergence at p is neither used nor true.

The exact constant normalization is
  integral_X exp(sigma(psi+Q_sigma))dnu0=1.               (2)
For |Q_sigma|<=B, the Taylor remainder divided by sigma is bounded by (sigma/2)(dL+B)^2 exp(sigma B). Its integral is O(sigma). Dividing (2)-1 by sigma gives
  tau_sigma=-integral_X(psi+w_sigma)dnu0+O(sigma).
Hence tau_sigma->-M and
  Q_sigma->w0-M uniformly on P1.                        (3)
All estimates apply to every sufficiently small sigma, so this is whole-family convergence.

Let s_sigma=psi+q_sigma and U_sigma=s_sigma-log(c0)/sigma=psi+Q_sigma. Then (3) gives
  U_sigma->s0=psi+w0-M
in L^1(X) and locally uniformly off D. More precisely, the residuals converge uniformly on the compact base; no norm subtracting infinities on D is claimed. Taking the supremum after adding the common psi is Lipschitz in the residual uniform norm. Thus A_sigma=sup_X U_sigma->S0-M. For c_sigma=exp(sigma sup_Xs_sigma),
  log(c_sigma/c0)/sigma=A_sigma->S0-M,
  c_sigma=c0 exp(sigma A_sigma)->c0,
  s_sigma-sup_Xs_sigma->psi+w0-S0
in the same potential topologies. The actual scalar error has been computed and retained.

notes.summary: Fixed singular-reference selection against all allowed singular subsolutions, with finite mass, retained ordinary type, exact stretching, and separated-sector order characterization.
notes.detailedSummary: Negative-constant truncation reduces arbitrary-singular greatestness to checked bounded comparison. Proves uniqueness in ordinary bounded type and all fixed-reference limits. The greatest mean-constrained critical subsolution and unique supremum-zero critical member are characterized only in the specified separated sector; universal zero-exponent uniqueness is not asserted.
notes.text:
Fixed-reference theorem: target C.

For every specified compact Hermitian Y, take q_sigma from n4 and put s_sigma=psi+q_sigma(x), canonically -infinity on D. Its bounded residual is eta-psh. Bounded local product expansion gives
  MA_eta(q_sigma)=N b^k(a omega_1+Dq_sigma) wedge kappa^k
                =exp(sigma(psi+q_sigma))N b^kH dW.
By n2 this is MA_theta(s_sigma). Therefore s_sigma is a genuine solution with f=N b^kH and has ordinary bounded type relative to psi and the model phi of n3.

This is the actual non-pluripolar product. There is no divisor mass. The factor exp(sigma psi)=ell^(sigma d) has value zero on D. The exponential density is the ordinary function exp(sigma s_sigma)f with that value, never a reciprocal infinite weight multiplied by a divisor current.

Greatestness holds against every allowed singular competitor. Let v be genuine theta-psh, v<=phi+C, and an exponential subsolution; permit arbitrary additional poles and even infinite total mass. By n2 and n3 write v=psi+r, with genuine eta-psh residual r, and
  MA_eta(r)>=exp(sigma r)F_sigma dW,
  F_sigma=N b^kH ell^(sigma d).
Choose a sufficiently negative finite constant A with exp(sigma A)||H||_infinity<=a. Since eta is positive, A is eta-psh and
  MA_eta(A)=N a b^k dW>=exp(sigma A)F_sigma dW.
The potential R_A=max(r,A) is bounded genuine eta-psh. On {r>A}, plurifine locality gives MA_eta(R_A)=MA_eta(r). On the complementary set {R_A=A}, the bounded contact inequality of n1 gives MA_eta(R_A)>=eta^N. These disjoint sets include the entire level set, so globally
  MA_eta(R_A)>=exp(sigma R_A)F_sigma dW.
Bounded strict comparison with q_sigma gives R_A<=q_sigma, hence r<=q_sigma. Adding the canonical psi proves v<=s_sigma everywhere. Thus arbitrary-singular greatestness is proved by bounded truncation, without importing a singular domination theorem.

If another solution has ordinary bounded type relative to phi, its residual is bounded by n2. Strict comparison in both directions in eta proves equality with q_sigma. The product background eta is strictly positive, admits the strict barrier 0, and meets all checked bounded comparison hypotheses. Closedness, factor symmetry, a bounded mass property on Y, and v_-(eta)>0 are unnecessary.

The measure has finite positive mass: its horizontal measure has total a, so
  N a(min b)^k <= integral_X MA_theta(s_sigma) <= N a(max b)^k.
Adding constants leaves the actual measure unchanged.

The whole-family computations in n4 establish
  v_sigma=s_sigma-sup_Xs_sigma -> v0=psi+w0-S0,
  s_sigma-log(c0)/sigma -> s0=psi+w0-M,
  c_sigma->c0,
  log(c_sigma/c0)/sigma->S0-M,
where M=integral_X(psi+w0)dnu0. Potential convergence holds in L^1(X) and locally uniformly off D. The exact limit equation is
  MA_theta(v0)=N b^k(aH/m)dW=c0 f dW,
with positive finite mass N a integral_P1 b^kH/m omega_1.

Since w0 is bounded and psi~phi, the limit has ordinary bounded type phi and exactly the canonical poles D. It belongs to the specified stretching class directly: choose C>=0 with v0>=phi-C, and for every real t>=1 take the genuine theta-psh potential a_t=phi-tC. Then
  t^(-1)a_t+(1-t^(-1))phi=phi-C<=v0,
including common poles. No unrestricted converse from zero-obstacle envelope equality is used. The same bounded-type argument also applies to s0.

For the separated order characterization, let u=psi+r(x)<=phi+C be a critical subsolution. Its residual is genuine a omega_1-psh on P1. The positive current mu=a omega_1+Dr has total a. Degree and non-pluripolar locality give
  MA_theta(u)=N b^k<mu> wedge kappa^k,
where <mu> is the one-dimensional non-pluripolar part, with <mu><=mu. The critical inequality, after division by b^k and integration over Y, gives <mu>>=(aH/m)omega_1. Its right side has total a. Therefore equality holds and mu has no lost polar mass. Thus D(r-w0)=0; the compact curve maximum principle and canonical representatives imply r=w0+C_r. Conversely all such constants give the critical equation.

The condition integral_Xu dnu0<=0 is now exactly C_r<=-M. Its greatest member is s0=psi+w0-M, of nu0-mean zero. The condition sup_Xu=0 instead forces C_r=-S0 and yields v0. This proves the separated-sector order characterization and normalized uniqueness, rather than inferring potential uniqueness from the scalar.

Additionally c0 is the largest critical coefficient among all subsolutions dominated by phi. For MA_theta(psi+r)>=c f dW with c>0, let B=sup r. The potential psi+r+log(c)/sigma-B is an exponential subsolution because psi<=0 and r<=B. Greatestness bounds it by s_sigma. Evaluate off D at a finite point of r and multiply by sigma. The uniform bound on q_sigma-log(c0)/sigma gives log c<=log c0 in the limit. The coefficient c0 is achieved by v0. This does not assert uniqueness of arbitrary nonseparated critical potentials.

notes.summary: Moving logarithmic references and data converge with independent rates; actual measures converge in total variation and limiting ordinary type is proved.
notes.detailedSummary: Uniform additive scalar barriers, Green estimates, and Taylor normalization identify every moving limit and scalar error. A common compact set controls moving suprema. No derivative convergence of b_j or relation between parameter and exponent rates is required. Model equations require positive parameters; convergence concerns the automatically positive tail.
notes.text:
Moving-reference theorem: target D.

Assume a_j->a>0, d_j->d>0, smooth positive b_j->b uniformly, and continuous positive H_j->H uniformly, with b smooth positive nonconstant and H continuous positive. Let sigma_j>0 tend to zero. The convergence statements concern the eventually positive tail a_j,d_j>0. To demand defined model formulas and equations at every initial index also requires positive a_j,d_j there; finite initial indices do not affect convergence. On the tail n5 supplies the greatest solutions s_j=psi_j+q_j(x). Also osc(b_j)>=osc(b)-2||b_j-b||_infinity>0 eventually, so the tail backgrounds are genuinely nonclosed by n2. No derivative convergence of b_j is required.

Set L=-log ell, W_j=H_j exp(-sigma_jd_jL), I_j=integral W_j, m_j=integral H_j, c0j=a_j/m_j and Q_j=q_j-log(c0j)/sigma_j. Eventually the positive parameters and m_j are bounded above and away from zero, and ||H_j||_infinity is bounded. The barriers of n4 apply index by index. Since
  0<=m_j-I_j<=sigma_jd_j||H_j||_infinity integral L,
eventually I_j>=m_j/2 and log(m_j/I_j)/sigma_j is uniformly bounded. The barrier residuals T(a_jW_j/I_j-a_j) are uniformly bounded by the Green estimate. Consequently ||Q_j||_infinity<=B independently of j. This crucial bound does not compare c0j and c0 on the exponent scale.

Write tau_j=integral Q_j omega_1 and w_j=Q_j-tau_j. The exact scalar equation yields
  w_j=Tg_j,
  g_j=c0jH_j exp(sigma_j(psi_j+Q_j))-a_j,
  integral g_j=0.
Off p, exp(-sigma_jd_jL)->1. The additive bound and parameter convergence give g_j->aH/m-a in every finite L^p by dominated convergence. Hence w_j->w0 uniformly. Density convergence is not uniform at p, where the exponential weight remains zero.

Let dnu_j=(H_j/m_j)dW. Integration gives
  integral exp(sigma_j(psi_j+Q_j))dnu_j=1.
Because |psi_j+Q_j|<=d_maxL+B and integral L^2 is finite, the Taylor estimate is uniform:
  0=integral(psi_j+Q_j)dnu_j+O(sigma_j).
The densities H_j/m_j converge uniformly; psi_j=-d_jL converges to psi in L^1 and L^2; and w_j converges uniformly. Therefore
  tau_j=-integral(psi_j+w_j)dnu_j+O(sigma_j)->-M,
  Q_j->w0-M uniformly on P1.
It follows that
  s_j-log(c0j)/sigma_j=psi_j+Q_j->s0
locally uniformly off D and in L^1(X). In particular ||psi_j-psi||_L1=|d_j-d| because integral L dW=1.

Moving suprema require a separate argument. Set A_j=sup_X(psi_j+Q_j). A fixed point with ell>0 supplies a uniform finite lower bound. Since d_j>=d/2 eventually, on {ell<epsilon} one has psi_j+Q_j<=(d/2)log epsilon+B. Choose epsilon so this lies below that lower bound. All maxima then lie in the common compact set {ell>=epsilon}. Local uniform convergence there gives A_j->S0-M. Thus the actual scalars satisfy
  c_j=c0j exp(sigma_jA_j)->c0,
  log(c_j/c0j)/sigma_j=A_j->S0-M.
Also v_j=psi_j+Q_j-A_j->v0 in L^1 and locally uniformly off D. None of these arguments restricts the relative rates of a_j,d_j,b_j,H_j and sigma_j.

The actual products have densities
  MA_theta_j(s_j)=MA_theta_j(v_j)
    =N b_j^k c0jH_j exp(sigma_j(psi_j+Q_j))dW.
All coefficient factors converge appropriately and are uniformly bounded. The exponential tends to one almost everywhere and is bounded above by exp(sigma_jB). Dominated convergence gives L^1 density convergence to N b^k c0H=c0f, hence total variation convergence. Each product is genuinely non-pluripolar with finite positive mass; no formal cohomological mass is substituted.

Ordinary type retention follows from the actual limit formula: v0=psi+w0-S0 has bounded residual relative to psi, and n3 proves psi~phi_{a,d}. Thus its ordinary type is phi_{a,d}, with exactly D as its pole set. The explicit stretching construction in n5 proves membership in E_env(X,theta,phi_{a,d}). This does not assume bounded comparisons between moving references, which generally fail when their logarithmic coefficients differ.

Each phi_j is separately the ordinary model in its own background. The bounded residual F_{a,d} in n3 is jointly continuous in positive (a,d) and x, including its matching circle and p. On a compact parameter neighborhood it is uniformly continuous. Hence F_{a_j,d_j}->F_{a,d} uniformly and phi_j=psi_j+F_{a_j,d_j}->phi_{a,d} in L^1 and locally uniformly off D. This identifies the moving reference limit directly.

For a_j=1+sqrt(sigma_j), moving scalar centering has finite error while centering by 1 diverges. Symbolic checks and small grid observations are distinguished from proofs.
notes.text:
Examples and centering obstruction: target E.

Represent P1 as the standard sphere with height t=2ell-1; reversing the axis does not change the integrals. Its Fubini–Study probability pushes t to the uniform distribution on [-1,1] by n4. Choose a=1, d=1/4, b=2+t, H=1. Then b is smooth, positive, nonconstant, and lies between 1 and 3. By n2 both backgrounds are strictly positive and genuinely nonclosed for every allowed Y.

Here m=1, c0=1 and g0=0, so w0=0. Also sup psi=0 and integral psi dnu0=(1/4)integral_0^1 log ell d ell=-1/4. Therefore the proved selection gives
  v0=psi,
  s0=psi+1/4,
  c_sigma->1,
  log c_sigma/sigma->1/4.
The centered and supremum-normalized limits differ even for this smooth positive density.

Take the primary Hopf surface Y=(C^2 minus {0})/<z->2z>. Dilation acts freely, properly discontinuously and holomorphically: a compact subset of the punctured space has radii bounded above and away from zero, so meets only finitely many of its dilates. Quotient charts give a smooth complex surface. Writing z=r xi, xi in S^3, the quotient identifies log r modulo log 2 and leaves xi fixed. Thus Y is diffeomorphic to S^3 x S^1, connected and compact; the annulus 1<=r<=2 is a compact fundamental region with its boundary spheres identified.

The form Omega=i sum_{l=1}^2 dz_l wedge dbar z_l/|z|^2 is smooth and strictly positive. Dilation multiplies numerator and denominator by 4, so it descends. On the fundamental annulus,
  Omega^2=8 r^(-4)dx_1 dy_1 dx_2 dy_2.
Since the Euclidean area of S^3 is 2 pi^2,
  integral_Y Omega^2=8(2 pi^2)integral_1^2 dr/r=16 pi^2 log 2.
Therefore kappa=Omega/(4 pi sqrt(log 2)) is positive Hermitian with integral kappa^2=1. Its exterior derivative is nonzero: differentiating r^(-2) and wedging with the Euclidean Kahler form gives a nonzero three-form in complex dimension two.

The obstruction to any Kahler metric is independent of this particular form. Elementary product cohomology gives H^2(S^3 x S^1,R)=0. A Kahler form alpha would therefore be exact, alpha=d beta. Since it is closed, Stokes gives integral alpha^2=integral d(beta wedge alpha)=0, contradicting positivity. Hence Y is not Kahler. The product P1 x Y is an actual compact complex threefold and cannot be Kahler, because a Kahler form would restrict to a Kahler form on its Y fiber.

Here k=2 and N=3. The actual selected zero-exponent measure is
  MA_theta(v0)=MA_eta(0)=3(2+t)^2dW,
and its mass is exactly
  3 integral_{-1}^1(2+t)^2 dt/2=3(4+1/3)=13.
There is no divisor mass. This is the selected limit’s mass; the ordinary model need not have the same mass in a nonclosed background.

Finally take a_j=1+sqrt(sigma_j), with d,b,H fixed and arbitrary sigma_j->0. Then c0j=a_j. By n6,
  s_j-log(a_j)/sigma_j->psi+1/4,
  log(c_j/a_j)/sigma_j->1/4.
Centering by the limiting scalar 1 instead adds log(1+sqrt(sigma_j))/sigma_j. For z=sqrt(sigma_j), log(1+z)/z->1, so this added constant is asymptotic to 1/sqrt(sigma_j) and tends to positive infinity. Thus the improperly centered potentials diverge at every fixed point off D, whereas the correctly centered family has a finite limit. Supremum normalization still converges to psi.

Program evidence is explicitly separate. verify.py symbolically checks the Green mean, log ell mean, model matching, and mass 13. With 2000 finite-volume cells, the fixed grid scalar errors at sigma=0.1,0.01,0.001 are 0.2319002923, 0.2479844199, 0.2497020267. For moving a they are 0.2274972745, 0.2478255101, 0.2496969397, whereas centering by 1 gives 2.9751961986, 9.7788434906, 31.3827706292. These non-exhaustive observations are consistent with the proofs but do not establish the limits. Discrete residual maxima are approximately 1.1–1.7 times 10^(-10); endpoint discretization remains a numerical limitation.

Deliverable and scope.

Notes n1–n7 contain the reconstruction: checked permitted analytic dependencies; arbitrary-pole divisorial removal and background assertions; exact full-product model and smaller-background envelope; Green formula and scalar asymptotics; fixed-reference greatestness and separated-sector order selection; moving logarithmic reference stability; and nonclosed examples including a non-Kahler threefold of selected mass 13. These remain unverified mathematical drafts. Source inspection and successful execution do not certify correctness.

All artifacts are in /workspace/research/native-workers/codex-Dn7cnk. Files n1.txt through n8.txt retain the ordinary proof notes. assemble_notes.py builds proof_notes.json with earlier-note supports. The existing input.json was preserved unmodified. verify.py performs six symbolic identity checks and ten small finite-volume observations. Run bash rerun.sh to rebuild numerical evidence and the note index without network access. Results are retained in verification_output.json and verification_stdout.txt; execution_record.json records the successful command and scope. The managed cloud runtime skill and non-secret network policy were read. Credentials were not inspected. No private proposed proof, frozen proof, previous native report or candidate article was read.

The result is the particular singular-reference and varying-logarithmic-reference regime proved above, for every specified compact Hermitian factor, with ordinary limiting type established directly. H is continuous positive, so this does not establish selection for arbitrary genuine L^1 data. The critical order characterization is the proved separated-sector characterization. Uniqueness of arbitrary nonseparated zero-exponent potentials is not asserted. Arbitrary model-reference stability and unrestricted original S05 remain open here.
